clue.text: Artist's triumph with unhurried smash hit

blocks.note: to triumph is to win
unhurried means going slowly
in baseball a smash hit that clears the fence is a home run, or homer

explanation.surface: A painter enjoys a leisurely, triumphant blockbuster success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' reads as 'Artist is': the painter Winslow Homer. 'Smash hit' looks like a show business success but is the baseball sense, a homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Winslow Homer was a celebrated nineteenth-century American painter, known for seascapes and watercolours.

clue.text: Exchange set after Nobel-winning dramatist shifts opening to finale

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the front and moved to the end of the name
after places the word before it second, following the playwright's altered name

blocks.note: Harold Pinter, playwright, Nobel laureate in 2005
to set something down is to lay it

explanation.surface: A trade-off set after a prize-winning playwright moves his opening scene to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright's initial travels to the end of his name, and the setting word follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Interplay is the give-and-take of mutual action between people or things, an exchange.

clue.text: Native Americans plead aloud

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to sue is to plead a case in court

explanation.surface: Indigenous people make an appeal out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a group of Native American peoples of the Great Plains, including the Lakota and Dakota.

clue.text: Approve a detective's exotic beast

blocks.note: to OK something is to approve it
taken as written
a private investigator

explanation.surface: A private eye signs off on a strange creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a rare striped forest relative of the giraffe from the Congo, an unusual animal.

clue.text: Where you don't want to wind up: stirring the oats

definitions.text: Where you don't want to wind up

indicators.note: porridge being stirred gets churned around, so its letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A cook warns against ending up stirring porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' could mean finish or be stirred; the definition means the place you would hate to find yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot seat is an uncomfortable position of pressure or responsibility nobody wants to occupy.

clue.text: Duck back to once again catch some sleep?

indicators.note: going back means the assembled string is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: the prefix meaning again
a snag is a catch or hidden drawback
REM, rapid eye movement, is a stage of sleep

explanation.surface: Someone ducks back to grab another nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb and 'catch some sleep' like a single idea; split it into a drawback and a sleep stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a narrow serrated bill.

clue.text: Recovery of traveler I misled

indicators.note: being misled means led astray, so these letters end up out of their proper places

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Finding a tourist who was given wrong directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval is the act of getting something back, which is what recovery means.

clue.text: Look over small jail

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the can is American slang for prison

explanation.surface: Inspecting a little prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to look it over quickly, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Bismarck, whether advancing or retreating

indicators.note: the word reads the same going forwards or backwards, so either direction gives the same name

blocks.note: the first name of Germany's Iron Chancellor

explanation.surface: The battleship Bismarck, or the general, seen in attack and in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition supplies the letters; the rest of the clue only observes that the name is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the Prussian statesman who unified Germany, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: A car, intact after a breakdown in a cold spot

indicators.note: something that has broken down falls apart and gets rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A car still in one piece after breaking down somewhere freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctica, the continent around the South Pole, is the coldest place on Earth.

clue.text: Announced something like ultracomplete meal

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the answer is judged by its sound

blocks.note: ultra- in ultracomplete is a word beginning attached to a stem

explanation.surface: Someone declares a feast to be more than complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultracomplete' is not a description of the meal: its 'ultra' is an example of a prefix, and prix fixe is pronounced the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A prix fixe is a restaurant menu of several courses offered at one set price.

clue.text: For example, Fleming is from the East

blocks.note: as in the sense 'such as'
Ian Fleming, the creator of James Bond

explanation.surface: Fleming, cited as an example, is said to come from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the East' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition; no letters are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The East here means the Orient, so something from there is Asian in origin.

clue.text: Namesake of London gallery, wearing jeans, is on the rise?

indicators.note: whatever is worn has clothing wrapped around it, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: Levi's, the denim brand
Henry Tate, sugar magnate, gave his name to the Tate gallery

explanation.surface: The man the Tate is named after, in denim, is doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rise' suggests a career going up; the question mark marks the literal sense of floating upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise and hover in the air as if by magic, so the verb fits literally.

clue.text: Unsuccessfully give a demo for Grand Theft Auto, e.g.

indicators.note: a demonstration that goes unsuccessfully goes wrong, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Botching a preview of a popular car-stealing title.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Theft Auto is a best-selling series of crime games played on consoles, so it is an example.

clue.text: Chats about work with Canuck's right wing interrupting slap shot, unfortunately

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its rightmost edge, its final letter
something that goes unfortunately goes awry, so these letters fall into a different order
to interrupt is to break into, so the single letter joins the other fodder

blocks.note: the last letter of Canuck, slang for a Canadian
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A Canadian hockey winger botches a hard shot, then discusses the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The hockey picture makes 'right wing' a player position; here it is the end of a word. A slap shot is a hard, swinging hockey shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is the idiom for discussing one's job, especially at a social occasion.

clue.text: Celebrities write six words as an afterthought

blocks.note: six in Roman numerals
a postscript, added after a letter is finished

explanation.surface: Famous people add a few lines at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities are very important persons, the people waved past the velvet rope.

clue.text: "Doctor, doctor — I spy China!"

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with something, so these letters are altered in their order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A 'Doctor, doctor' joke in which the patient complains of seeing crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface parodies the 'Doctor, doctor, I feel like…' joke format; the first 'Doctor' is the indicator, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician is a medical doctor, especially one practising medicine rather than surgery.

clue.text: Read Pynchon in reverse to nab professional friskers?

indicators.note: to nab is to catch, so the letters are caught inside the run of text
going in reverse means the run of text is read from right to left

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Reading a novelist backwards to catch the airport security staff who pat you down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across 'reaD PYNchon'. The question mark admits the definition is playful: New York police officers frisk suspects for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Police Department's officers stop and search people, so they are frisking professionals.

clue.text: In the final moments, come back from the side

blocks.note: late means near the end
to rally is to recover after falling behind

explanation.surface: A team stages a comeback in the dying minutes from the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting comeback makes 'from the side' look like part of the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, in a direction across rather than straight ahead.

clue.text: Second attempt, like eating watermelon at first

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is placed inside another
at first means only the opening letter of the fruit is used in the insertion

blocks.note: to take to something is to like it
the first letter of the fruit

explanation.surface: Having another go, like someone biting into a watermelon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a comparison; it is the phrasal verb take to, which wraps the initial of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Take two is the film director's call for the second shooting of a scene, hence another try.

clue.text: Oppose Canada's first flag maker

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the country's name is kept

blocks.note: the initial of the country
Betsy Ross, credited with sewing the first American flag

explanation.surface: Resisting the designer of the maple leaf flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The Canadian setting points to the maple leaf, but the flag maker is the American seamstress of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone is to go against them or thwart their wishes.

clue.text: Summer program for outrageous behavior

blocks.note: first meaning: an organised summer holiday for children
second meaning: deliberately exaggerated, theatrical style

explanation.surface: A summer scheme designed to curb children's outrageous conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the American summer retreat for children and an affected, over-the-top style.

clue.text: That's disgusting! Education, having broken up family, began to take effect

indicators.note: a group that is broken up is split apart, leaving room for other material in its middle

blocks.note: one's kin are one's relatives; this word is split open
an exclamation of revulsion
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gross remark about schooling splitting a family before something kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces go together between the first letter of the family word and its last two.
explanation.definitionFit: When a drug or a policy kicks in, it starts to work, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Starts to confer (or converse) over alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one from each word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Beginning to discuss something over a boozy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcoholic drink' reads as one phrase, but 'alcoholic' only gives a letter; the answer is not alcoholic at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: Chattering on, we produced boredom

indicators.note: chattering is talking, so the words are taken by their spoken sound

blocks.note: the two words run together as spoken

explanation.surface: Our endless prattling made everyone tired of listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The French loanword is pronounced roughly 'on-wee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless weariness and lack of interest, a literary word for boredom.

clue.text: Quote me the wrong way, incorporating a trajectory for understanding

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the quotation is read from its end
to incorporate is to take into a body, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: to quote is to cite
a trajectory is the path a projectile follows

explanation.surface: Someone misquoted asks for a little sympathy about a flight path.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed quotation is itself a word, emetic, and the path goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An empathetic person shares and grasps the feelings of others, so is understanding.

clue.text: Carpenter's item is no trouble

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for no
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A woodworker's piece of kit causes no bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No trouble' reads as one phrase meaning easy; split it and each word gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter hammers metal spikes into wood to join pieces together.

clue.text: Probes former Middle Eastern group's allowances

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
the Palestine Liberation Organization
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: Investigations into the expenses of a defunct regional body.
explanation.definitionFit: Explorations and probes are both searching investigations into the unknown, a plural noun synonym.
